candidate: HYP-RC6 — Causal Attribution & Reversible Topology Switching (CARTS)

hypotheses.claim: Causal-credit topology is distinct from semantic, propagation, invalidation, selection/workspace, physical and authority topology.
hypotheses.prediction: Outcome-level broadcast credit produces more false reinforcement/attractor concentration than path/item-scoped credit under matched tasks.
hypotheses.falsifier: Broad credit performs equally or better under preregistered shift/poison controls without higher concentration or false association.

hypotheses.claim: UNKNOWN causal credit should not be treated as positive credit.
hypotheses.prediction: Receipt-gated/uncertain updates preserve rare-context accuracy better than unconditional positive propagation after distribution shift.
hypotheses.falsifier: Uncertainty gating provides no robustness benefit or merely suppresses useful learning.

hypotheses.claim: A topology candidate and the live topology reference are separate semantic/authority objects.
hypotheses.prediction: Versioned candidate construction plus atomic live-ref switch prevents torn topology states under crash injection.
hypotheses.falsifier: Real durable/runtime tests show equivalent torn-state frequency or hidden dependencies make old/new separation invalid.

hypotheses.claim: Destruction-free/versioned topology change is not intrinsically safe.
hypotheses.prediction: Bad but fully recoverable topology versions can cause wrong routing/outage when activated without effect-time validation.
hypotheses.falsifier: Constructive activation cannot cause consequential harm in realistic maintenance/agent workloads.

hypotheses.claim: Topology activation should use bounded canary/health evaluation for consequential adaptive changes.
hypotheses.prediction: Canary admission plus rollback reduces bad-update exposure relative to direct repoint while retaining a measurable fraction of beneficial updates.
hypotheses.falsifier: Canary signal does not predict real harm/benefit or rejection cost dominates on target workloads.

hypotheses.claim: Credit scope should bind causal stage receipts from candidate formation through outcome/re-entry.
hypotheses.prediction: Credit accuracy improves when item/path/route/assembly scope is derived from stage-resolved receipts instead of endpoint success alone.
hypotheses.falsifier: Stage-resolved attribution has no predictive/robustness value beyond scalar reward.

hypotheses.claim: Query-adaptive propagation/routing may be useful while topology-learning updates remain slower and more conservative than per-query activation.
hypotheses.prediction: Fast contextual routing with slower validated policy/topology promotion beats either frozen routing or direct online live mutation on quality × robustness.
hypotheses.falsifier: One timescale is sufficient under target traces.

hypotheses.claim: Authority topology cannot be inferred from learning credit or live-topology popularity.
hypotheses.prediction: MCAAT-style host-only permits block reward/salience/workspace values from self-authorizing topology or external effect switches.
hypotheses.falsifier: Equivalent containment is achieved without explicit authority separation under adversarial tests.

hypotheses.claim: Cross-platform topology optimization requires semantic equivalence plus matched Linux/Android evidence.
hypotheses.prediction: Android-optimal placement/routing choices will not universally dominate Linux and some resource decisions will reverse across platforms.
hypotheses.falsifier: Matched traces show stable ordering across platforms and loads.

hypotheses.claim: A fully consistent topology switch can still be cognitively wrong; atomicity and utility validation are orthogonal.
hypotheses.prediction: Atomic switch tests can pass while shuffled/poisoned topology variants degrade task outcomes.
hypotheses.falsifier: Consistency receipts suffice to predict cognitive utility on target tasks.
